assumptions.summary: Work years proxy ability because ability and knowledge are unavailable; salary level proxies ambition and department membership because those data are unavailable.
No employee is fired; each simulation step is one month and social influence from a departure applies in the next month.
ICM is assumed to reach maximum output at 85% fill of 370 positions; six levels are defined by salary.
Recruitment cost is paid for a new person, while qualified staff are trained annually and initial training is included in recruitment cost.
HR may adjust retained staff, recruit after churn and assign entrants to vacant positions; the GA treats only assignment as its intervention.
Productivity is proportional to salary proxies and penalized by staffing imbalance; because output data are unavailable the objective switches to cost minimization.
Chromosome operators model promotions but not firing or demotion, and overfull levels are infeasible.
The baseline uses 85% on-job rate, 10% hiring, 18% churn, 500 people, random initial graph/traits and five averaged simulations.
The HR-health case sets 30% churn in experienced supervisors and junior managers and forbids recruitment into those middle levels.
N=200, K=2000, MR=0.4 and CR=0.1 are chosen from local GA experiments; the information and department additions are not simulated.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: The Summary supplies paper-internal Tasks 3-5 outputs, a 370-person setting, three graph types, loyalty/intimacy and the GA route.
Introduction and assumptions establish the management object, temporal convention, proxies, position levels and cost convention.
Figures 1-5 define people, position and bipartite relations; Figure 6 layers their monthly snapshots.
Table 1 defines six salary-based levels; Figures 7-10 supply loyalty/intimacy, assignment and churn-process interfaces.
Productivity and cost formulas use salary, staffing counts, structural coefficients, training and recruitment terms without released output data.
Table 2 and Figures 11-13 define chromosome symbols, feasibility and promotion-only genetic operators.
Baseline inputs include 18% churn, 10% recruitment, 500 people, random graph/traits, five simulations, population 200 and 2000 GA iterations.
Table 3 records the monthly 24-month baseline; Table 4 and Figures 15-17 compare churn, recruitment, direct cost, indirect cost and feasible regions.
Table 5 records level-specific staff flows; Figures 18-20 supply local GA tuning and a conceptual multilayer extension.

dependency_graph.handoff: The static relation graphs supply initial loyalty, intimacy, hierarchy and assignment context.
The loyalty/intimacy state and transition matrix supply assignment-aware updates.
Updated assignments and states define the monthly dynamic HCN and churn inputs.
Churn and vacancies supply staffing and structural terms for productivity and cost.
Total cost becomes the fitness objective for the restricted genetic assignment.
Baseline assignment and event traces supply the budget comparator.
Baseline cost traces supply the matched churn/recruitment scenario comparison.
Scenario and middle-level vacancy results supply the conditional HR-health reading.
The HR-health and cost limits motivate local parameter analysis and conceptual extensions.

independent_extensions.summary: Release consented people, position, friendship, hierarchy and eligibility edge data with their temporal refresh rules.
Estimate loyalty and intimacy from longitudinal outcomes rather than treating culture, expectation and similarity as opaque functions.
Calibrate and test the transition matrix, position-gap relationship, skipped-move composition and assignment costs.
Freeze seeds, departure sequencing, probability clipping, simultaneous events, recruitment capacity and graph refresh policy.
Validate staffing/structure productivity and cost proxies against observed organizational outcomes and units.
Publish genetic populations, feasibility results, fitness traces and comparisons with demotion/firing-capable alternatives.
Repeat baseline and scenario simulations with raw paths, uncertainty, capacity constraints and a declared 80% decision tolerance.
Test whether direct-cost savings at higher churn persist when salary, replacement quality, worker harm and structural stability are jointly measured.
Evaluate promotion opportunity, loyalty, wellbeing, fairness and capability with observed employee data before adopting the middle-level policy.
Replicate parameter selection across seeds, scenarios and stopping tolerances before using N, K, mutation or crossover defaults.
Collect information-flow, department, leadership and same-level-transfer data and specify the coupling before implementing a multilayer model.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Separating friendship, hierarchy and assignment prevents one graph from being mistaken for all human-capital relations.
The missing-output admission makes the cost objective honest about the change in decision criterion.
Direct and indirect costs must remain separate to avoid turning a local cost drop into a high-churn recommendation.
Table 5 anchors the middle-level conclusion in promotion flows rather than an aggregate health label.
The information and department extensions are useful precisely because the source stops before claiming evidence it does not have.

language_observations.summary: The reusable human writing style is not a phrase list: it reveals a concrete management difficulty, admits what cannot be measured, introduces a proxy and its behavioral premise, gives a local equation or visual example, reads a table/curve into a next action, and leaves the conclusion bounded by its evidence.

the Summary exposes a graph-to-decision route before detail: Move from three relation objects to static and dynamic networks, separate own and social churn, hand assignment to a genetic algorithm, report scenario outputs, and end with parameter and information-layer limits.

the Introduction repeats the route as section-level handoffs: Name what each section constructs or decides, so loyalty, intimacy, churn, cost, assignment, applications, tuning, and team science arrive in dependency order.

an unmeasurable employee trait is replaced only after the gap is disclosed: State that ability, knowledge, ambition, or department membership cannot be observed, then use work years or salary level as a tractable proxy and name the behavioral premise that makes it usable.

a behavioral timing premise becomes a simulation ordering rule: Choose one month as the state interval, use a notice example, and delay influence from a departing neighbor until the following month before writing churn formulas.

different relation meanings are separated before graph integration: Keep friendship independent of leadership, represent positions as a tree, represent person-position eligibility as a bipartite graph with a training state, and only then combine the three structures.

a local mechanism proceeds from definition to formula to worked visual example: Define loyalty or intimacy in ordinary language, introduce the transformation or assignment matrix, and show how a two-employee promotion changes the loyalty vector.

network changes are followed by an explicit manager-authority boundary: List no-churn, churn-and-vacancy, and new-entry states, then identify recruitment, reassignment, and the genetic assignment loop as the actions available to HR.

missing output data force a narrower optimization target: Begin with the profit objective, disclose that staff output is unavailable, split organizational performance into staffing and structural terms, and switch to minimizing a constructed cost.

generic algorithm mechanics are rewritten as domain-specific operators: Map genes to training, six levels, absence, and departure; reject over-capacity chromosomes; and restrict mutation and crossover to promotions because firing and demotion were excluded.

simulation inputs are exposed before the results are interpreted: List fill, hiring, churn, population, random initialization, repetition count, and GA settings, while distinguishing data- or experience-based parameters from experiment-selected ones.

a long monthly table is compressed into a two-year budget claim: Read own and following churn, recruitment, and cumulative cost columns, compare annual rates with the initial settings, then sum recruitment and training costs on the source's sigma scale.

one scenario is read through two outcome classes instead of a single optimum: Hold the staffing target visible, show direct cost rising then falling with salary exposure, show indirect cost rising with structural instability, and retain the conflict in the conclusion.

a visual classification turns two rates into a bounded decision region: Sweep churn and recruitment from zero to forty percent, classify fill and structure outcomes with distinct markers, and draw a region boundary for the eighty-percent target.

an extreme middle-level case is interpreted through level-specific flows: Use a no-middle-level-recruitment scenario, read churn, promotion, recruitment, and ending headcount by level, then connect fresh promotion rates to the conditional loyalty mechanism.

a local search trace leads to a deliberately conservative parameter choice: Identify an iteration plateau near one thousand, choose twice that value, fix one genetic rate while sweeping the other, and select the observed local minima.

an omitted mechanism becomes a conditional layer rather than a completed result: Acknowledge that information flow is absent, explain why team performance could depend on it, and place information beside relationship and position networks without rerunning the model.

a structural mismatch is converted into concrete future model changes: Name department membership, leadership, same-level transfer, and department capacity as missing objects, and state how each would alter loyalty, intimacy, or productivity.

claimed strengths are immediately narrowed by source-specific weaknesses: Name the three graphs, timestamp, simulation, transformation, genetic assignment, and cost split, then admit assumption dependence and mismatch between the organizational graph and structure table.

results_trace.summary: Across 24 months Table 3 totals 14 following-churn, 120 own-reason churn and 75 recruits; the source reads annual churn near 19% and recruitment near 12% against 18% and 10% inputs.
The reported two-year baseline budget is 38.2 sigma recruitment plus 127.08 sigma training, or 165.28 sigma.
For 25% churn the source gives 22% recruitment and 617.64 sigma direct cost; for 35% churn it gives 31% recruitment and 533.66 sigma direct cost while warning of structural instability.
Figures 16-17 show rising indirect cost and classify 0-40% churn/recruitment settings by 80% fill and structure quality.
Table 5 reports 66.7% and 53% fresh-promotion rates in experienced supervisors and junior managers under the middle-level churn case.
The parameter section chooses N=200, K=2000, MR=0.4 and CR=0.1 from the paper's local experiments.
The source proposes information and department-aware extensions, then explicitly names assumption dependence and graph-table mismatch as weaknesses.

source_quality.summary: All 21 physical pages were read in order twice and visually reviewed. The paper starts from three organizational relations, uses proxies and delayed monthly state changes to create a dynamic human-capital network, switches from unavailable profit to a cost proxy, restricts a genetic assignment to promotions, interprets cost/feasibility/HR-health scenarios, and stops the information and department extensions at their missing-data boundary.

decisions: how to represent three relations, how state changes reach HR, how to constrain assignment, how to read direct/indirect cost, what evidence is required before deployment
inputs: 370-person organization, human-capital management need, positions, churn/recruitment setting, cost/training convention and HR scenarios
outputs: static/dynamic HCN, churn and recruitment simulation, cost-minimizing assignment, budget/scenario/health readings, local GA settings and conceptual multilayer extension

title: Human Capital Management in Organizations
unresolved_questions: The Summary reports budget and churn-scenario values, but they remain outputs of the paper's own assumed network and optimization process.
Work years as ability, salary level as ambition, no firing, one-month timing, next-month influence and the 85 percent maximum-output premise are assumptions rather than observed employee mechanisms.
Initial loyalty and intimacy are undefined functions of culture, expectation, acquaintance time and interest similarity; no employee-level calibration or privacy protocol is released.
The transition matrix and loyalty multiplier have no empirical values, admissible range, asymmetry rule or evidence that promotion causes the stated change.
The same-position recursion is visually degraded and uses an assumed mean-promotion mechanism; skipped promotions are composed without testing path dependence.
Intimacy is rescaled from salary-level gaps, which may confound friendship with hierarchy and lacks observed relationship outcomes.
The assignment and loyalty-vector algebra is inspectable, but eligible edges, assignment costs, simultaneous moves and a machine-readable transition matrix are absent.
Social churn probability has no seed, observed transmission coefficient, probability clipping, simultaneous-departure policy or released monthly event trace.
Productivity and both cost components are constructed proxies because staff output is unavailable; coefficient provenance, sigma units and validation outcomes are missing.
The genetic representation rejects overfull levels and encodes promotion only, but gives no feasibility proof, demotion/firing alternative, quality bound, seed, or reproducible fitness trace.
Random graphs, random traits, an 18 percent churn target, a 10 percent hiring rate and five averaged simulations do not establish a calibrated baseline.
Table 3's 19 and 12 percent readback is close to the assumed rates, but raw runs, confidence intervals, salary cost and the sigma cost source are not released.
The fall in direct cost at high churn reflects lower salary exposure inside the proxy and cannot outweigh the paper's own rising structural instability without a common validated outcome.
The zero-to-forty-percent feasibility map is a gridded internal classification without uncertainty, recruitment-capacity constraints or an external organizational comparator.
Table 5's loyalty and motivation claim depends on assumed qualification, no middle-level recruitment and promotion rates; worker outcomes were not measured.
The choices K=2000, mutation 0.4 and crossover 0.1 come from local figures without seeds, repeated sweeps, a convergence tolerance or out-of-sample comparison.
The information layer and department adjustments are conceptual extensions; no information-flow edges, coupling, transfer history or departmental capacity data are supplied.
The source itself admits assumption-dependent values and mismatch between the organizational graph and structure table, so neither representation is externally validated.

writing_logic.summary: management pressure -> three relation graphs -> dynamic monthly network -> cost-minimizing GA -> task results -> local tuning -> information layer
section roadmap -> assumptions/proxies -> graph construction -> dynamic state -> cost fallback -> applications -> extensions
unmeasurable ability/ambition -> work-year/salary proxy -> stated premise -> limited model scope
timing example -> next-month influence -> state restriction -> churn formula
friendship/position/assignment distinction -> three graph forms -> static HCN -> monthly layers
loyalty/intimacy definition -> formula -> matrix -> worked example -> dynamic handoff
network change type -> vacancy or entrant -> HR authority -> reassignment/recruitment action
missing staff output -> productivity/cost proxy -> minimize cost -> GA fitness
generic GA -> chromosome symbol meaning -> capacity rejection -> promotion-only operator -> approximate assignment
parameter ledger -> randomized baseline -> Table 3 rate/cost readout -> two-year budget
same fill target -> direct-cost curve -> salary mechanism -> indirect structural curve -> tradeoff
two-rate grid -> visual feasibility classes -> 80% target region -> bounded conclusion
middle-level churn stress -> level flow table -> promotion rate -> conditional loyalty/health claim
iteration plateau -> conservative K -> controlled rate sweeps -> local GA settings
missing information flow -> new layer -> conceptual diagram -> no simulated result
